entries.title: How the Cubs' James Triantos is blocking out the impending trade deadline
entries.summary: <p>The Aug. 3 trade deadline is hours away. The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" target="_blank" >Cubs</a> badly need <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/30/cubs-mlb-trade-deadline-pitching-starting-rotation-matthew-boyd-shota-imanaga-colin-rea-david-peterson-javier-assad-tarik-skubal" >starting pitchers and could use help in the bullpen</a>. Whenever a potential trade candidate is scratched from a start, the news spreads on social media and ignites speculation about impending moves.</p><p>It’s hard for anybody who’s invested in baseball not to pay attention and think about which big names will be in new places by Monday night. Yet rookie infielder James Triantos, a potential trade chip who could be directly impacted if the Cubs do something, isn’t using brain space on the subject.</p><p>“It’s not worth it to me to stress out over stuff that I can’t control like that,” Triantos told the Sun-Times before the Cubs’ game Saturday against the Yankees. “So, I just focus on showing up at the field and being ready to go every single day. This is a great opportunity to have, and I just want to take advantage of it.”</p><p>Sparingly used since getting recalled July 24 from Triple-A Iowa, Triantos made his first big-league start Saturday, batting ninth and serving as the Cubs’ designated hitter against New York lefty Max Fried. Before Saturday, Triantos had just two at-bats.</p><p>That didn’t seem to sour him on the value of his first look at major-league life with the Cubs.</p><p>Triantos is eager to soak up whatever information he can during his first stay in the big leagues. He said the experience has been “amazing,” taking bits of info from his new teammates with shiny resumes and track records of producing at the highest level. He’s observing how consistent the veterans are with their routines and preparing, both mentally and physically.</p><p>“It’s everything I can dream of,” Triantos said. “It’s such a great opportunity to learn and be around the guys. It’s fun to win.”</p><p>For additional pointers on maximizing this time, Triantos said he’s spoken a lot with former Cubs prospect Owen Caissie, one of his best friends. Caissie was called up Aug. 14 last year.</p><p>“He learned a lot from these guys,” Triantos said. “Just asking him the ins and outs and what I should be ready for and everything like that.”</p><p>That connection might turn out to be ironic or fitting, depending on the point of view.</p><p>Caissie didn’t have long to apply what he learned for the Cubs. He played in 12 games and had 26 at-bats but that was the sum of his Cubs tenure, which ended when he was traded to the Marlins as part of the Edward Cabrera deal.</p><p>A second-round pick in 2021, Triantos has steadily climbed through the Cubs system. A right-handed hitter with good contact skills, Triantos has attributes that could be attractive to a suitor looking for prospects that should be ready to contribute in the major leagues now or soon.</p><p>And there’s also the matter of where Triantos could play for the Cubs. In six minor-league seasons he has 38 home runs, so he doesn’t profile as a hitter who would fully transition to a corner outfield spot. He is further blocked by Nico Hoerner, Dansby Swanson and Alex Bregman, who will be at second base, shortstop and third base, respectively, for the foreseeable future.</p><p>None of these permutations are bothering Triantos. He doesn’t have X/Twitter on his phone and doesn’t look for information or chatter with his name in it.</p><p>“I get paid to live out my dream. It’s not that hard,” Triantos said of ignoring the noise. “This is what I love to do. This is my job. This is my favorite thing to do. It’s all I’ve loved to do forever.”</p>

entries.title: Robert Lewandowski scores twice in victorious home debut with Fire
entries.summary: <p>Robert Lewandowski scored two goals, including the winner, in his home debut for the Fire, helping them beat Charlotte 2-1 on Saturday at Soldier Field.</p><p>Lewandowski, who made the move from FC Barcelona in a two-year deal with Chicago, equalized in the 20th minute off a screamer from outside the box that tied the game at 1.</p><p>He connected on his second goal of the night in the 68th minute with a go-ahead shot to the bottom left corner to seal the win for the Fire (9-6-2), who played their first home match in over two months.</p><p>Pep Biel gave Charlotte (7-7-4) an early lead with a shot from the right side of the box on an assist from Idan Toklomati.</p><p>Charlotte pushed for an equalizer late and earned a corner in stoppage time, but Chicago held on to preserve the one-goal lead.</p><p>Charlotte entered the match unbeaten in its last two games, but dropped its third straight against the Fire.</p><h3><b>Up next</b></h3><p>Charlotte: Takes on Pumas UNAM in Leagues Cup group stage play on Tuesday.</p><p>Chicago: Visit Club Necaxa in Leagues Cup group stage play on Thursday.<br></p>

entries.title: Woman shot in Austin carjacking
entries.summary: <p>A 36-year-old woman was shot during a carjacking early Saturday in Austin, Chicago police said.</p><p>Officers responded to a call of a person shot at about 12:37 a.m. along the 4600 block of West Fifth Avenue, police said.</p><p>The woman was getting out of her car when a man approached, fired shots and demanded access to her vehicle before fleeing, according to police.</p><p>The woman suffered a gunshot wound to the back and was treated at the scene by the Chicago Fire Department personnel, police said. She was taken to Mount Sinai Hospital in good condition.</p><p>Area Four Detectives were investigating.</p>

entries.title: Federal judge tosses Trump administration lawsuit seeking full access to Illinois voter rolls
entries.summary: <p>A downstate federal judge has rejected an effort by President Donald Trump’s administration to obtain full access to Illinois’ voter registration database, including sensitive personal data on more than 8 million residents statewide.</p><p>The Justice Department’s request for the voter rolls “to ascertain Illinois’s compliance” with federal law isn’t a legitimate reason for demanding the vast trove of data, “as it does not relate to any suspected violation of voting,” Judge Colleen Lawless wrote in a 14-page opinion issued Friday.</p><p>The decision from Illinois’ Central District court in Springfield marked the 19th ruling nationwide against lawsuits filed by the Trump DOJ <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2025/12/19/illinois-voter-rolls-voting-lawsuit-president-trump" target="_blank" ><u>over the past year</u></a> in what it has called an effort to ensure election integrity.</p><p>Trump has long falsely claimed rampant voter fraud led to his 2020 election loss to former President Joe Biden, though cases of fraud have proven <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/democracy/2024/05/15/election-disinformation-democracy-solutions-project" target="_blank" ><u>exceedingly rare anywhere in the country</u></a>.</p><p>“If the Attorney General could simply justify his demand with a statement of any purpose whatsoever, the requirement that he specify his purpose (and his basis) would be pointless and it would provide him with unfettered authority to demand voting records,” Lawless wrote.</p><p>Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul said the ruling underscores the fact “voters can remain confident that our elections are fair and secure.”</p><p>“The Trump administration’s demand for Illinois’ unredacted voter registration list is part of the president’s ongoing efforts to undermine and sow doubt in U.S. elections,” Raoul said in a statement. “But in Illinois, we are focused on ensuring voters’ access to the ballot box while protecting their personal information.</p><p>“The Constitution is clear: States have authority to administer and regulate elections,” Raoul continued. “Courts have consistently ruled that the Department of Justice’s attempts to commandeer unredacted voter registration lists are unlawful.”</p><p>DOJ officials couldn’t immediately be reached for comment.</p><p>The Trump administration requested Illinois’ full voter database last July, and the Illinois State Board of Elections provided voters’ names, addresses and ages at registration — but not dates of birth, ID numbers or social security numbers, as limited by state law.</p><p>That prompted the DOJ to sue “to protect American citizens from vote dilution,” but local election authorities are responsible for most of that information, and handing it over would violate federal privacy law, too, Illinois officials argued.</p><p>The American Civil Liberties Union of Illinois hailed the decision, and Ami Gandhi, director of the Midwest Voting Rights Program with Chicago Lawyers’ Committee for Civil Rights, called it “a critical victory for the privacy rights of every Illinois voter.”</p><p>“The federal government's attempt to seize sensitive personal records was an unprecedented overreach designed to intimidate voters and fuel false narratives about our election systems,” Gandhi said in a statement. “By rejecting this demand, the court has sent a clear message that our democratic process will not be weaponized to harass or suppress Illinois voters, particularly naturalized citizens and people returning home from incarceration who are disproportionately targeted by these efforts.”</p>

entries.title: David Peterson strong again in Cubs' 5-2 win over Yankees
entries.summary: <p>When pitcher<b> David Peterson </b>joined the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> after a June 25 trade with the Mets, the move wasn’t expected to change the path of the pennant race or give his new team an ace. <b>Edward Cabrera </b>and <b>Ben Brown </b>had just landed on the injured list, joining <b>Justin Steele</b>, <b>Cade Horton </b>and <b>Jameson Taillon</b>, meaning the Cubs just wanted somebody who was healthy.</p><p>Peterson, who had a 6.09 ERA in 68 innings with the Mets, qualified. He <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/06/26/cubs-david-peterson-trade-mets-starting-rotation-craig-counsell-all-star-pitcher" >was available</a>, not terribly expensive to get and experienced.</p><p>“We were wondering who was going to start a game for us,” manager <b>Craig Counsell </b>said. “That’s where we were at.”</p><p>Peterson has done more than just stabilize the rotation and eat innings. He’s been a key part of the staff, which he showed again in the Cubs’ 5-2 win Saturday over the Yankees.</p><p>Peterson went 6 1/3 innings, giving up two runs (one earned) while matching a season high with eight strikeouts. He has a 1.52 ERA in his last four outings, and has completed at least five innings while allowing two or fewer runs in five of his six Cubs starts.</p><p>As for what Peterson’s changed since joining the Cubs, he said there’s “nothing huge or new.” Instead, it was restoring old patterns and using his lower body more efficiently to take stress off his arm, which allows better command and pitch shapes.</p><p>“That’s kind of the biggest thing, and then just kind of tweaking things as we go and finding spots we can get better,” Peterson said.</p><h2><b>In the clutch</b></h2><p>Despite Peterson’s work, the Cubs trailed 2-1 in the bottom of the seventh. <b>Nico Hoerner </b>changed that with a leadoff solo home run that survived the brisk wind blowing in.</p><p>With two outs, <b>Pedro Ramirez </b>pinch-hit for <b>James Triantos </b>and worked a walk, keeping the inning alive for <b>Pete Crow-Armstrong</b>. Facing lefty <b>Brent Headrick</b>, Crow-Armstrong pulled a slider into the right field corner for a triple that brought in Ramirez and put the Cubs ahead.</p><p>“I know it’s spring training, but [Ramirez] definitely made a big impression in spring, just with how he carried himself,” Hoerner said. “He’s humble but confident and enjoys the game, has a good sense of humor. He’s going to have a really great career, so he’s been huge for us.”</p><p><b>Seiya Suzuki </b>completed the Cubs’ seventh-inning rally with another run-scoring single, though he was called out when he over-slid second and was tagged.</p><p>“That was a stretch of some really good at-bats that inning,” Counsell said.</p><h2><b>Cabrera’s rehab</b></h2><p>Cabrera<b> </b>(left hamstring strain) made the first start of his rehab assignment Friday for Triple-A Iowa. Cabrera pitched 1 2/3 innings and gave up three runs, but more importantly than his numbers, Cabrera came through the outing healthy, throwing 43 pitches and topping out at 98.8 mph.</p><p>“We’ll move to the next step [and] increase the pitches,” Counsell said. “He kind of showed he hadn’t been out there for a month, but that’s expected and normal. Just keep building from here.”</p><p>Cabrera’s next start for Iowa will be Wednesday, and he is expected to need another after that before rejoining the Cubs.</p>

entries.title: First pitch arrives in Springfield for Women's Pro Baseball League: 'We're ballplayers, too'
entries.summary: <p>SPRINGFIELD — The Jimmy Dugan character portrayed by Tom Hanks might have told his Rockford Peaches women's baseball team in the 1992 classic “A League of Their Own” that there’s “no crying in baseball.”</p><p>But there were tears of joy shed at the inaugural Women’s Pro Baseball League game Saturday in Springfield, where real-life Rockford Peach Maybelle Blair, 99, threw her ceremonial first pitch from a wheelchair to kick off <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports/2026/07/31/womens-pro-baseball-comes-home-to-illinois-paving-the-way-for-next-generation-of-ballplayers" >the sold-out season opener</a>.</p><p>More than 4,000 poncho-wearing fans packed the rain-soaked stands, singing along to Shania Twain’s “Man! I Feel Like a Woman!” as the Los Angeles Queens went to bat against the New York Heights after a 90-minute weather delay.</p><p>Both teams came stacked with star power. Japanese pitcher Ayami Sato and former Little League champion and outfielder Mo’Ne Davis represented LA, while Team USA’s powerhouse duo of outfielder Kylee Lahners and catcher Denae Benites anchored the Heights.</p><p>Nine-year-old Lena Shackleford of Virginia attended the historic game two years after participating in a catching lesson with Benites in Washington D.C.</p><p>Decked out in royal-blue Heights gear, Shackleford said she dreams to be a catcher like Benites, who hit the first, and so far only, home run of the season.</p><p>“There's only like two times I've been in a tournament that's all girls, so I'm kind of used to being the only one.” Shackleford said. “It feels really great to know that there are other [girls] out there.”</p><div class="Enhancement" entries.title: White Sox acquiring Mariners starter Luis Castillo for reliever Seranthony Dominguez, two prospects
entries.summary: <p>ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — The White Sox are going for it. To what degree, we’ll see.</p><p>They made their first splash before the trade deadline at 5 p.m. Monday by acquiring Mariners right-hander Luis Castillo late Saturday for reliever Seranthony Dominguez and prospects Nolan Jones and Boston Smith. The Sox also are picking up the rest of Castillo’s contract.</p><p>Castillo, 33, is a three-time All-Star who can add length and playoff experience to a rotation in need of both. Outside of Sean Burke, Sox starters generally are done by the fifth inning, and none has pitched in the postseason. But Castillo’s 5.06 ERA in 20 games this season (17 starts) is the worst of his career.</p><p>He figures to get more run support with the Sox, who rank ninth in the majors with 522 runs. The Mariners are 28th with 447. Castillo received three runs or fewer of support in 15 starts and allowed four runs or fewer 13 times.</p><p>Castillo might take rookie left-hander Noah Schultz’s spot in the rotation. After two stinkers coming out of the All-Star break, Schultz delivered five innings of one-run ball Saturday against the Rays. But that one run was one too many in a 1-0 loss. Schultz followed opener Jordan Hicks, who threw a perfect first.</p><p>After rumblings that the Sox were unlikely to make such a move, general manager Chris Getz dealt a quality prospect in Smith, a catcher who ranks 15th overall in the Sox’ system, according to MLB.com.</p><p>Catcher isn’t a strength in the organization. Kyle Teel has missed much of the season with injuries, and Edgar Quero and Drew Romo aren’t providing enough offense. At three minor-league levels this season, Smith has a 1.037 OPS with 22<br>home runs.</p><p>Jones, an outfielder acquired from the Guardians in June, also has some pop, though he isn’t ranked among the Sox’ top 30 prospects. In Triple-A with both franchises this season, Jones has an .807 OPS with 14 homers.</p><p>Dominguez, whom the Sox signed to a two-year, $20 million contract in the offseason, lost his closer job about a month ago but has started to come on. He had one of his best innings of the season Saturday, striking out two and throwing 11 of 14 pitches for strikes in a perfect seventh against the Rays. </p><div class="PageListL" data-module entries.title: Review: Geese soars above the haters as the controversial New York rockers debunk the myths haunting the band
entries.summary: <p>In the year since the release of its latest album “Getting Killed,” Geese has been in the crosshairs of many a music critic and music snob.</p><p>The New York rockers have been accused of being industry plants, scene interlopers and marketing manipulators at best. Their “Saturday Night Live” debut was picked apart. Their family lines were investigated for possible record label moles. A band nowadays apparently can’t actually be good and have a sudden rise before being prematurely autopsied.</p><p>But at Lollapalooza Saturday, Geese spread its wings and properly debunked the myths that keep haunting the band. </p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-170000" The quality of the show is ‘up in the air,’ so to speak.”</p><p>To the aforementioned music snob, it probably is ammo in the band’s argument. For the casual fan, no one seemed to know any difference. A sizable crowd flocked over to the Allianz stage to catch the controversial act, though it was unclear if that all was truly for Geese or hangers on for Olivia Dean who headlined on the adjoining T-Mobile stage right after.</p><p>“Who’s on after us?” asked Winter. Some responded correctly. “Nobody!” and “Who cares?” said others. In either case, it was a win for the quartet who are just weird and mysterious enough to turn heads.</p><p>The music rose to the occasion, with Winter’s inner Lou Reed and Julian Casablancas shining on songs like on “2112,” “100 Horses” and “Cowboy Nudes,” matched by the on-point playing of fellow guitarist Emily Green, bassist Dominic DiGesu and drummer Max Bassin. They all operated with great cohesion and rule-breaking gumption, no more so than in the brutal blues rocker “Trinidad” that could be their best work.</p><p>When <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/music/2025/12/17/review-cameron-winter-rockefeller-chapel-chicago-show-heavy-metal" >Winter headlined the Rockefeller Chapel</a> at the University of Chicago last December under the guise of his solo album “Heavy Metal,” he proved his gifts, just himself and a piano. But on the Lolla stage with the full band, it’s tenfold. His charisma as a front man is undefinable. It may not be in line with the fervent fans who hail him as this generation’s Kurt Cobain. Then again, Courtney Love is a very vocal supporter of him and the band so there’s that.</p><p>Formed in 2016, Geese comes from the holy grail of Brooklyn, an untouchable lineage to some, but the quartet wears the Television, Velvet Underground and Strokes influences well on songs like fan favorites “Taxes,” “Bow Down” and “Cobra” without coming off as pantomime. Throw in a little Leonard Cohen on slow peak songs “Au Pays du Cocaine” and “I See Myself.” Maybe some Henry Rollins on bar brawler “Jesse.” Who could hate any of that? entries.title: Harvey police identify 2 victims in fatal shooting
entries.summary: <p>Authorities have identified two people found fatally shot inside a far south suburban home Thursday.</p><p>The victims were identified as Jwon L. Martin, a 46-year-old Harvey woman, and Aaron Jones, a 50-year-old Harvey man, according to a spokesperson for the Harvey Police Department. </p><p>Police were called to a home near 150th Street and Vine Avenue, where officers found the two victims with gunshot wounds, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-suburbs/2026/07/30/harvey-dog-shooting-150th-vine" target="_blank" >Harvey police said Thursday</a>.</p><p>Both victims were pronounced dead at the scene, police said.</p><p>Two dogs had also been shot. Authorities said one dog died and the other was in critical condition as of Thursday.</p><p>The department said the investigation was active and ongoing.</p><p>Anyone with information is asked to contact the Harvey Police Department Detective Division at 708-331-3030 ext. 226.</p>

entries.title: Heavy rain disrupts commutes, Lollapalooza as more flooding hits Chicago area
entries.summary: <p>Chicagoans might get a break from the rain Sunday after the latest round of soggy weather disrupted traffic, flooded more homes and upended the schedule at Day 3 of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/lollapalooza/2026/08/01/heavy-rains-delay-opening-of-doors-at-lollapalooza-on-day-3" >Lollapalooza</a>.</p><p>Forecasters expected drier conditions arrive into Sunday with highs in the mid-70s, according to the National Weather Service.</p><p>NWS meteorologist David King said Saturday's highest rainfall totals in the area fell in eastern Kendall County, where up to 4 inches of rain fell, while parts of far northeastern Will County and eastern DuPage County from Downers Grove to Elmhurst were soaked with 2 to 3 inches.</p><p>"A constant stream of intermittent showers" prompted flash flood warnings across the area, King said.</p><p>"It's been a good soaking rain for much of the area," he said. "If you're traveling, be a little more cautious and allow more room between you and the vehicle ahead."</p><p>Chicago's Office of Emergency Management and Communications was coordinating with city departments and other agencies in response to the storms, according to spokesperson Mary May.</p><p>Officials were still assessing the impact of the rainfall that came on the heels of several other storms this summer that have caused headaches for thousands of residents with <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/weather/2026/07/27/weather-storms-heat-wind" >flooding and seepage</a>. Four <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/news/2026/07/28/storms-flooding-tornadoes-damage-worker-missing-power-outage" >tornadoes</a> were confirmed in the weather system that raked the area last week. </p><p>Flooded roads posed hazards Saturday, as Illinois State Police responded at about 7:45 a.m. to southbound Interstate 55 at Joliet Road, with a report of water across all lanes, Sgt. Jason Wilson said. </p><p>There weren't major roadway closures, crashes or stranded vehicles linked to flooding as of Saturday evening, but images posted to social media showed part of a retaining wall appeared to have collapsed at the Lawrence Avenue exit on the Kennedy Expressway.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr"><a href="https://x.com/hashtag/ChicagoScanner?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#ChicagoScanner</a> <a href="https://x.com/hashtag/Chicago?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#Chicago</a> <a href="https://x.com/hashtag/ChiTraffic?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#ChiTraffic</a> <br><br>Inbound Kennedy Expy I-90 at the Lawrence exit the outer retaining wall to the exit ramp has collapsed onto the right embankment of the inbound lanes<br><br>Ramp currently closed for inspection, no current lane closures on the Kennedy but that… <a href="https://t.co/Wy3qmDdRbw">pic.twitter.com/Wy3qmDdRbw</a></p>— WindyCity Weather and News (@WindyCityWxMan) <a href="https://x.com/WindyCityWxMan/status/2083595405367882071?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">August 1, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>In Clarendon Hills, about 3 inches of rain fell over a two-hour period, resulting in flooded and impassable roadways, flooded yards and several reports of flooded basements, Village Manager Paul Dalen said. entries.summary: <h2>Moon alert</h2><p>Avoid shopping (except food and gas) and important decisions from 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. After that, the moon moves from Pisces into Aries.</p><h2>Aries (March 21-April 19)</h2><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-290000" name="html-embed-module-290000"></a><div class="HoroscopeStarbox HoroscopeStarbox_five"> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_container"> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> <svg class="HoroscopeStar"><use xlink:href="#icon-star"></use></svg> </div> <div class="HoroscopeStarbox_description"> <p>A <b>so-so</b> day</p> </div> </div> <style> .HoroscopeStarbox { background: #f8f8f8; display: flex; align-items: center; } .HoroscopeStarbox_container { display: grid; grid-gap: 5px; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr; padding: 20px; width: 40%; min-width: 160px; max-width: 200px; } .HoroscopeStarbox_description { padding: 20px; font-family: var(--font-1); font-size: var(--body-2); } .HoroscopeStarbox_container svg { object-fit: cover; aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; width: 100%; } </style> </div> </div><p>Today is a mixed bag. entries.title: Person shot through window of Belmont Cragin home
entries.summary: <p>A 41-year-old person was wounded in a shooting Friday evening in Belmont Cragin, Chicago police said.</p><p>The victim was inside a home in the 2100 block of North Mobile at 7:33 p.m. when someone fired a shot through a window, according to police.</p><p>They were taken to Loyola University Medical Center in Maywood in serious but stable condition, police said. </p><p>Police said late Saturday that the victim knows the shooter.</p><p>Area Five Detectives were investigating, police said.</p>

He has yet to say whether he will run for mayor again.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Jeremy Battle/Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>“His administration has become a revolving door of senior leadership, making it harder for the city to get things done, reducing confidence in the city — and the whole world sees it,” Giannoulias told the Sun-Times in a recent, wide-ranging interview.</p><p>Effective leadership requires “forming coalitions and working with people,” and Johnson is “failing at this,” Giannoulias said.</p><p>“Jousting with the governor. Making demands at the end of session rather than working earlier to develop policy and build support… His attempt to raise property taxes was rejected by the City Council 50-to-0 and the City Council passed a budget 29-to-19 when he failed to back off the job-killing corporate head tax,” Giannoulias said.</p><p>“A mayor who cannot move an agenda through Springfield and City Council is having difficulty… looking out for the interest of Chicagoans.”</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/city-hall/2026/07/28/mayor-brandon-johnson-acting-cfo-steve-mahr-resigns" >abrupt resignation </a>of the city's chief financial officer, Steve Mahr, and his top deputy — just as Chicago prepares to host a crucial investors conference and the City Council gears up for a grueling election year budget season — is the most recent example of the “revolving door” at Johnson’s City Hall, Giannoulias said.</p><p>“He hired a longtime veteran of the city in Rich Guidice to have a steady hand when he got elected, and he left less than a year into the administration. Police Superintendent [Larry] Snelling resigned with less than a year left in this administration, which is the most challenging time of year for the police,” Giannoulias said.</p><p>“Three sister agencies went without a leader for more than a year: CPS, CHA and CTA. And after going nearly ten years without a credit downgrade, Chicago has… been downgraded by three rating agencies in just over a three-year period.”</p><p>Giannoulias condemned as “dangerously irresponsible” the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/chicago-school-board/2026/07/30/chicago-school-board-approves-budget-that-reverses-layoffs-but-counts-on-shaky-state-funds" >Chicago Board of Education’s decision </a>to roll the dice and approve a nearly $10 billion budget that counts on $150 million from Springfield, along with a $285 million tax increment financing surplus that the City Council has not approved.</p><p>He called it yet another sign that the Chicago Teachers Union, which bankrolled and staffed Johnson’s 2023 mayoral campaign, is calling the shots in his administration.</p><p>“Instead of adopting the [Chicago Public Schools] CEO’s proposed budget, which included some staffing cuts, the CTU-linked members jammed through this alternative budget, which avoids any hard choices about structural changes. That’s not leadership,” Giannoulias said. “I will work with the board president to advocate for more funding. But we have to start with a more responsible budget… Glittery possible revenue is not responsible.”</p><h3>The prospect of school closings</h3><p>Giannoulias said a more responsible school budget must confront the financial elephant in the room — 145 schools with more empty seats than students.</p><p>If elected mayor, he’s vowing to tackle that problem, but with a community- and parent-driven process “paired with real investment in students and staff... not closures imposed from downtown with little notice.”</p><p>“Past closures, particularly in 2013, were handled in a way that broke trust with Black and Latino communities, and that history can’t be ignored or repeated,” Giannoulias said.</p><p>Johnson points to former Mayor Rahm Emanuel’s decision to close 50 schools in one fell swoop in 2013 as an example of glaring disinvestment in South and West Side communities.</p><p>But at the risk of being portrayed as Emanuel 2.0, Giannoulias said, “You have to make tough decisions… A school with too few students cannot offer the full range of programs… The student experience is not the same. It’s not a healthy environment for 70 or 80 students to be in a school that was built for 1,500. It’s not good for anyone.”</p><p>A former state treasurer, Giannoulias got his start in politics as a basketball-playing buddy of Barack Obama. He played professional basketball in Greece, where he learned valuable lessons about competiveness, teamwork and how to, as he put it, "surround yourself with players that are better than you so that you can get better."</p><p>It’s no surprise, then, that former two-term president is Giannoulias' political mentor and role model.</p><p>“What he did outstandingly well — and the lesson he taught me at every step for every office he ran, he said, 'Make sure you surround yourself with people who are way smarter than you at every stop of the way.' That’s been like buried in my brain,” Giannoulias said. “I look for the most capable, talented people who have an inherent understanding of that particular challenge.”</p><p> Giannoulias, 50, has four daughters under the age of 10. He said he and his wife struggled with the decision to dive into a grueling campaign for a "brutal" job with greatly diminished powers, enormous problems and no easy solutions.</p><p>Chicago is facing a $90 million mid-year shortfall, a $1 billion-plus budget gap in 2027 and a $36 billion pension crisis with two of the four city employee pension funds hovering dangerously close to bankruptcy.</p><h3>A ‘very tough’ decision</h3><p>"It's really difficult when you have four little girls that you love with all your heart and you want to spend time with them. [It's] very personal, very tough for me," Giannoulias said.</p><p>"But I love this city and I care about this city, and I want them to see their father working to be part of the solution. As cheesy and idealistic as it sounds, I want them to look up and say, 'One day when the city was struggling, my dad was one of the many, many people who did his best in a transparent and an honest way to fight for this city.'"</p><p>With only $631,309 in his campaign fund to nearly $22 million for Giannoulias, Johnson is leaning heavily on social media and on the power of incumbency, along with the free media that comes with it.</p><p>He is expected to portray Giannoulias as a repeat of Emanuel — a captive of the very people who would be most affected by the embattled mayor’s mantra to “tax the rich.”</p><p></p><p>Giannoulias hopes to blunt some of those attacks by joining Johnson in the campaigning for a 3% tax on annual income over $1 million. </p><p>But he knows that won't blunt the political arrows coming his way.</p><p>"I'm a big boy. I can take it," Giannoulias said.<br></p>

entries.title: Why new Blackhawks prospect Xavier Villeneuve might be a future star — or might be a bust
entries.summary: <p><a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> fans might fall in love with Xavier Villeneuve in a few years and spend the next decade watching in awe as he dances around the ice at the United Center. </p><p>Or they might never see him at all.</p><p>One of those outcomes is relatively likely for Villeneuve, the first of the Hawks’ two <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/06/27/blackhawks-draft-picks-2026-analysis-xavier-villeneuve-ryan-roobroeck?_gl=1*1ssgk49*_up*MQ..*_ga*ODAwOTY3OTc2LjE3ODQxNDA3Mjc.*_ga_K0F0MB46T8*czE3ODQxNDA3MjYkbzEkZzAkdDE3ODQxNDA3MzAkajU2JGwwJGgw" target="_blank" >boom-or-bust draft picks</a> early in the second round.</p><p>The 5-11, 163-pound defenseman draws comparisons to budding Canadiens star Lane Hutson, who was a second-round pick, too. That’s obviously the Hawks’ dream scenario.</p><p>But for every Hutson, there’s a Nicolas Beaudin, one of the Hawks’ biggest draft busts of recent years. That fact isn’t lost on anyone, including Alexandre Jacques, Villeneuve’s coach last season with Blainville-Boisbriand of the QMJHL.</p><p>‘‘[Xavier is] not like a, let’s say, 6-4 player that’s big and strong . . . and you know it’s a sure thing when you draft him,’’ Jacques said. ‘‘You don’t expect him to become a superstar, but you know he can play on the third line, so it’s a safe pick.</p><p>‘‘For Xavier, it’s like you’re hitting a home run. He’s either going to be a Lane Hutson or he’s not going to play. It’s hard to project the future for this type of guy.’’</p><p>For the Hawks, the risk makes sense because they don’t need a third-pairing plug-in. They have other prospects with decent odds of developing into that type of player.</p><p>What they do need is what every team needs: star power. And Villeneuve has way more of that than anyone else who was still available at No. 34 overall.</p><p>‘‘He was just one of those guys that really popped for me when I met him in person,’’ Hawks general manager Kyle Davidson said.</p><p> ‘‘With how he talked about [hockey], even just knowing about the league, you can tell he loves the game and loves the sport. I just felt the passion oozing out of him. That gives you belief he’s going to do everything possible . . . to become the player he can be.’’</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr"><a href="https://x.com/hashtag/Blackhawks?src=hash&ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">#Blackhawks</a> second-round pick Xavier Villeneuve: <a href="https://t.co/9seWt4hE6V">pic.twitter.com/9seWt4hE6V</a></p>— BHF (@BlackhawksFocus) <a href="https://x.com/BlackhawksFocus/status/2070894664316498239?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">June 27, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3><b>Road to here</b></h3><p>Villeneuve’s dad, Alexandre, passed that passion to his son, who started playing at 4 while growing up in Quebec.</p><p>There was never a specific moment when Villeneuve realized he might have a future in hockey because he operated that way from the start, even though he was the youngest player on every team because of his September birthday.</p><p>‘‘It’s going to sound cocky, but it was always my dream and I always believed in it, even though you’re 9 years old,’’ Villeneuve said. ‘‘My expectations and standards were always pretty high to achieve that goal. I’m not there yet, but I think it’s going well.’’</p><p>It was going particularly well in January, as Villeneuve had racked up 36 points in 35 games for Blainville-Boisbriand while also improving his defensive play. Jacques felt comfortable giving Villeneuve defensive-zone starts and difficult matchups, which he hadn’t received previously, and NHL scouts were noticing.</p><p>Then a hip injury sidelined Villeneuve for more than two months, and he failed to rediscover his rhythm in two regular-season and 17 playoff games after returning. He especially struggled defensively.</p><p>‘‘The 2.5 months without playing kind of caught up to him,’’ Jacques said. ‘‘In the playoffs against big guys, it was a little tougher for him. . . . He’s smart enough [that] he knows he’s not going to go defend body-to-body, strength vs. strength. He’s got to defend with his edges and speed.’’</p><p>Said Villeneuve: ‘‘It was not a good season for me. I think he said it in a more polite way, but it didn’t go the way as planned.’’</p><p>He considered sitting out the end of the season not to jeopardize his NHL draft stock, and he arguably should have. He might have been a first-round pick. The Hawks, however, were happy about how it panned out.</p><p>At development camp after the draft, Villeneuve was transparent about the fact his hip still wasn’t 100%, but it should be by the start of the season.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-2f0000" name="image-2f0000"></a> <picture at Boston University, which he chose in part because <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2022/7/2/23166096/lane-hutson-jack-devine-nhl-draft-prospects-chicago-barrington-glencoe-hockey" target="_blank" >Hutson</a> exploded into a top prospect there.</p><p>‘‘Being in Montreal, everyone loved the Habs, so they were drawing the comparisons [between Hutson and me],’’ Villeneuve said. ‘‘As I got older, [given] what he’s doing right now, people started to really compare us. But what he’s doing right now is unbelievable. Hopefully I can get there soon.’’</p><p>Hawks scouting director Mike Doneghey also likes the BU path for Villeneuve, especially because the same coaching staff that molded Hutson remains in place.</p><p>Jacques no longer will be involved with Villeneuve’s development, but he did share some advice.</p><p>‘‘[He needs to improve] his play under pressure, his puck recoveries under heavy forecheck and being able to play in tight areas under pressure,’’ Jacques said. ‘‘He’s got the ability, skills and edges to do it. Now it’s about doing it on a consistent level. </p><p>"[Retrieving] 50/50 pucks in the corners after rebounds, to be good at it, he’s going to have to do it his way and not try to overpower players.’’</p><p>The relatively light college schedule will give Villeneuve more gym time to gain weight and strength. Doneghey hopes he eventually can achieve a ‘‘thicker build’’ in the mold of <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2025/12/22/blackhawks-matt-grzelcyk-steady-mentor-artyom-levshunov-nhl" target="_blank" >Matt Grzelcyk</a>, probably around 180 pounds.</p><p>Villeneuve thinks he might grow another inch or two because his dad is 6-1. That would be unusual but not unprecedented at his age.</p><p>He’s a self-described ‘‘hockey geek’’ who watches a lot of NHL games, a surprising rarity among prospects nowadays. On nights off, he often would choose a Western Conference matchup to watch after the Canadiens, focusing on top defensemen such as Quinn Hughes and Cale Makar.</p><p>‘‘I’m not comparing myself to them, but there’s so much I can learn from watching those guys,’’ Villeneuve said.</p><p>Said Jacques: ‘‘[Xavier] is going to be able to do things at the offensive blue line that we had never seen before, but now it’s starting to be a trend in the NHL with the Hugheses and Hutsons of this world.’’’</p><p>Executing those moves requires ample confidence in addition to ample talent, and that trait is one in which Villeneuve really stands out. </p><p>Jacques called it a ‘‘certain cockiness’’ that any athlete needs to make it to the pros, and he sees that in his former player.</p><p>It will take years to see whether Villeneuve does make it, but he hasn’t been deterred at all by his setback this spring. He’s getting right back to work.</p><p>‘‘Showing up, doing all the extras — for me, that’s where the confidence comes from,’’ Villeneuve said. ‘‘Because that move that I’m going to do that sounds crazy to some people, I’ve done it probably 25,000 times before.’’</p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Ex's passing is just a reminder that he was a jerk
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> After a nearly 20-year marriage, my first husband, "Lloyd," told me his feelings for me had changed. He said we needed "some time apart," but he didn't want a divorce. He immediately went to a lawyer and executed a financial settlement for me, still insisting he wasn't going to file for divorce. Six weeks later, I bought a house and moved. Two weeks later, Lloyd's son told me my husband moved a woman in with him two days after I moved out. Obviously, we divorced.</p><p>In time, I remarried and was very happy for 13 years until my husband died. I took care of him for the last three years. A year later, my older brother became ill, and I went to help him 300 miles away. It also turned into a nearly three-year stay.</p><p>I have been back home for only a year and a half now. I just received a text from a friend of Lloyd's telling me Lloyd has passed away. None of Lloyd's family contacted me, nor did they let me know his brother had died a while back. I have been so hurt by this man. After I moved, he told many lies. He said that I had been cheating, etc., and literally turned the whole community against me. When the true story came out, a lot of people apologized for treating me so badly.</p><p>I feel indifference toward my ex. The bad memories with him far outweigh the good ones, and I don't want to go to his funeral. It would feel two-faced because I lost all respect for him many years ago. Am I wrong for not acknowledging his death? — <i>MOVING ON IN THE SOUTH</i></p><p><b>DEAR MOVING ON:</b> You certainly are not wrong. People attend funerals in order to pay their respects and emotionally support the grieving family. Your presence is not required at this one. Lloyd's family would not welcome it, and neither would the woman who helped to break up your marriage. On that day, do something you would enjoy, ideally with friends who support you.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> Two years ago, my mother bought a pair of diamond earrings for us to split. She wears one every day, and I wear the other. She tried doing the same thing with my older sister about 20 years ago, but after my sister lost her diamond earring for the second time, they mutually agreed to give up.</p><p>Last summer, my mother gave me a box of old jewelry, odds and ends. I found two diamond earrings that looked similar but weren't from the same pair, so I took them — who doesn't like diamonds? Now I am realizing they're likely Mom's half of the pairs she split with my sister. Can I wear them? I have a place for each, but would it be an act of bad faith to horn in on what was originally their tradition? — <i>BEJEWELED IN NEVADA</i></p><p><b>DEAR BEJEWELED:</b> Your mother gave you the box of old jewelry. The items were hers, but now they are yours. Your sister lost the mates to those earrings and the tradition ended. Your sister should have no claim on them. Wear them and enjoy them without guilt.</p><p><i>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren, also known as Jeanne Phillips, and was founded by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 69440, Los Angeles, CA 90069.</i></p><p>Abby shares more than 100 of her favorite recipes in two booklets: "Abby's Favorite Recipes" and "More Favorite Recipes by Dear Abby." Send your name and mailing address, plus check or money order for $16 (U.S. funds), to: Dear Abby, Cookbooklet Set, P.O. Box 446, Kings Mills, OH 45034-0446. (Shipping and handling are included in the price.)</p>

entries.summary: <p>Handicapping the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>’ 53-man roster before Monday's first padded practice of training camp — and four weeks before cut day:</p><h3>OFFENSE (25 keepers/44 total)</h3><p><b>Quarterback (3/4)</b></p><p><b>They’re on the team:</b> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/08/01/bears-qb-caleb-williams-must-keep-climbing-no-matter-how-it-goes-with-offensive-line-this-season" target="_blank" >Caleb Williams</a>, Tyson Bagent, Case Keenum<br><b>Work to do:</b> Miller Moss<br><b>The big question:</b> Can they finish each other’s sentences yet? For the second-straight season, the Bears will have the exact same three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster — and the same quarterbacks coach.<br><b>Number to know:</b> 27 — Snaps taken by Bagent since Williams’ arrival.</p><p><b>Running back (3/6)</b></p><p><b>They’re on the team:</b> D’Andre Swift, Kyle Monangai, Roschon Johnson<br><b>Work to do:</b> Salvon Ahmed, Coleman Bennett, Brittain Brown<br><b>The big question:</b> What exactly does Johnson do? He played 667 offensive snaps in two years under Matt Eberflus — and four snaps last season under Ben Johnson. He helps on special teams, but doesn’t the coach want more juice out of his third running back?<br><b>Number to know:</b> 34 — Carries by Ahmed in 2022-23 while playing for new Bears running backs coach Eric Studesville as a member of the Dolphins.</p><p><b>Tight end (4/7)</b></p><p><b>They’re on the team:</b> Cole Kmet, Colston Loveland, Sam Roush, Nikola Kalinic<br><b>Work to do:</b> Stephen Carlson, Qadir Ismail, Hayden Large<br><b>The big question:</b> Does Theo Benedet count as a tight end? If his coach uses the Canadian tackle as an extra blocker again, the Bears can probably get by carrying three traditional tight ends.<br><b>Number to know:</b> 2 — Famous former NFL relatives in Ismail's family: his dad is Qadry ("The Missile") and his uncle is Raghib ("The Rocket").</p><p><b>Wide receiver (5/11)</b></p><p><b>They’re on the team:</b> Rome Odunze, Luther Burden II, Kalif Raymond, Zavion Thomas, Jahdae Walker<br><b>Work to do:</b> Maurice Alexander, Kaden Davis, Kyron Hudson, Omari Kelly, JP Richardson, Scotty Miller<br><b>The big question:</b> Do the Bears value Miller’s experience? He won a Super Bowl with Tom Brady and played alongside Aaron Rodgers last year. He doesn’t play special teams, though, which hurts his case to make the team.<br><b>Number to know:</b> 4.28 — The rookie Thomas ran a 4.28-second 40-yard dash, the third-fastest of any player at the NFL Scouting Combine.</p><p><b>Offensive line (10/16)</b></p><p><b>They’re on the team:</b> Braxton Jones, Joe Thuney, Garrett Bradbury, Jonah Jackson, Darnell Wright, Logan Jones, Theo Benedet, Luke Newman, Jordan McFadden, Jedrick Wills Jr.<br><b>Work to do:</b> Kiran Amegadjie, Caden Bennett, Kyle Hergel, Jaren Kump, Mason Murphy, Ozzy Trapilo. Trapilo will start on the Physically Unable to Perform list and is likely to miss most of the season.<br><b>The big question:</b> What to do with Amegadjie? The 75<sup>th</sup> overall pick in 2024 has been relegated to afterthought status. Asked about left tackles, general manager Ryan Poles praised Jones, Wills and Trapilo. Catching himself, he eventually added “and Kiran as well” — a sign he’s not top-of-mind.<br><b>Number to know:</b> 105 — Career starts by Bradbury, the presumed starting center, in seven seasons. He’s never come off the bench.</p><h3>DEFENSE (25/43)</h3><p><b>Defensive line (9/15)</b><br><b>They’re on the team:</b> Montez Sweat, Austin Booker, Gervon Dexter, Grady Jarrett, Dayo Odeyingbo, Daniel Hardy, Neville Gallimore, Kentavius Street, Shemar Turner. Turner is on the PUP list but is expected to return during training camp.<br><b>Work to do:</b> James Lynch, Jordan van den Berg, Jonathan Garvin, Jamree Kromah, Jayden Loving, Jeremiah Martin<br><b>The big question:</b> How much can Odeyingbo contribute? He posted eight sacks in the first 14 games of 2023. In 28 games since, he has four.<br><b>Number to know:</b> 73 — Pro Football Focus graded Jarrett their 73<sup>rd</sup>-best interior lineman last year. The injury-riddled season was his first of a three-year, $42.8 million deal.</p><p><b>Linebacker (6/11)</b><br><b>They’re on the team:</b> Devin Bush, T.J. Edwards, D’Marco Jackson, Ruben Hyppolite II, Jack Sanborn, Keyshaun Elliott. Edwards is on the Non-Football Injury list and Elliott is on PUP, with both expected to return soon.<br><b>Work to do:</b> Tony Fields II, Joe Rhattigan, Nephi Sewell, Wayne Matthews II, Noah Sewell. Noah Sewell is on PUP and isn’t expected to be healthy by the start of the season.<br><b>The big question:</b> Can Elliott play special teams? The Bears like the rookie’s instinctive tackling but he didn’t play on kicking downs at Arizona State.<br><b>Number to know:</b> $30 million — What the Bears are paying Bush over the next three years, more than he made in his first seven in the NFL.</p><p><b>Cornerback (6/10)</b><br><b>He’s on the team:</b> Jaylon Johnson, Tyrique Stevenson, Kyler Gordon, Josh Blackwell, Malik Muhammad II, Jaylon Jones. Gordon is on PUP without a firm return date.<br><b>Work to do:</b> KC Eziomume, Dallis Flowers, Dontae Manning. Terell Smith<br><b>The big question:</b> What will the Bears do if/when Gordon gets hurt again? Jones and safety Cam Lewis have been rotating at the slot corner in camp.<br><b>Number to know:</b> 8 — The league-high takeaways by cornerback Nahshon Wright last season before the Bears let him leave for the Jets in free agency.</p><p><b>Safety (4/7)</b><br><b>He’s on the team:</b> Coby Bryant, Dillon Thieneman, Cam Lewis, Elijah Hicks. Hicks is on PUP but should return soon.<br><b>Work to do:</b> Anthony Johnson Jr., Skyler Thomas, Gervarrius Owens<br><b>The big question:</b> How quickly can the starters gel? The Bears spent a first-round pick on one and their largest free-agent deal of the spring on the other. The pressure’s on to make an impact quickly.<br><b>Number to know:</b> 7 — Interceptions, since moving to safety two years ago, by Bryant. He had none in two years as an NFL cornerback.</p><h3><b>SPECIAL TEAMS (3/4)</b></h3><h3></h3><p><b>He’s on the team:</b> K Cairo Santos, P Tory Taylor, LS Luke Elkin<br><b>Work to do:</b> LS Beau Gardner<br><b>The big question:</b> Do they grab a veteran long snapper after cut day? There will be one available if Elkin and Gardner — the latter won the Patrick Mannelly Award at Georgia last year — don’t grab the job.<br><b>Number to know:</b> 100 — Percent of extra points made by Santos last season, the first time since 2014 he went perfect in a complete season.<br><i>•NOTE: The Bears have 91 players because Taylor, an Australian, has an international player roster exemption.</i></p>

entries.title: Man dropped off at St. Bernard Hospital with fatal gunshot wound
entries.summary: <p>A man suffering from a fatal gunshot wound to his chest was dropped off at St. Bernard Hospital in Englewood early Sunday, Chicago police said. </p><p>The man, whose name and age have not been released, was taken to the hospital at 326 W. 64th St. around 5:40 a.m. He was later pronounced dead, according to police. </p><p>Details surrounding the incident, including where the shooting happened, are unknown, police said.</p>

entries.title: Review: Olivia Dean is ‘all about love’ in feel-good Lollapalooza performance
entries.summary: <p>If <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/lollapalooza/2026/08/01/review-charli-xcx-delivers-jaw-dropping-drama-amid-made-for-movies-downpour" >Charli xcx’s headlining set</a> was a moody arthouse film, fellow Brit Olivia Dean’s Lollapalooza moment was the feel-good classic you screen on a cozy rainy day — except on Saturday, fans waded in a Grant Park swamp to sing, get emotional and share space with the beloved crooner.</p><p>The night was Dean’s first headlining a festival in the U.S., an occasion she welcomed with soul-baring singalongs, bits of wisdom and candor between songs, and a fireworks show that brought a level of connectedness to a mud-covered crowd.</p><p><b></b> She reflected on having first played Lollapalooza two years ago, telling fans she’d been in tears all day processing her place as Saturday’s headliner.</p><p>“To be headlining this year is just crazy and truthfully I’ve been crying all day because I feel so privileged to do this,” Dean confided to the massive crowd that blanketed the field in front of the T-Mobile stage. <b></b></p><p>The London native’s bright smile and honeyed, slightly raspy, pitch-perfect vocals felt like a balm at the end of a rainy, chilly day. She glided across the main stage in two different silver dresses as her voice floated over her immaculate seven-piece band, rounded out by a horn section and two angelic background singers. Bordering the platforms on the stage were large petals, with Dean often at the center, like a bright blossom.</p><p>It has been a whirlwind year for Dean, 27, since releasing her sophomore album, “The Art of Loving,” last September. The record “changed her life,” she said, sending her career on a nonstop upward trajectory, with viral fame, No. 1 singles and a Grammy Award for Best New Artist.</p><p>Among those accolades is achieving the longest-running United Kingdom No. 1 single in history with Sam Fender, thanks to their “Rein Me In” collaboration, which has reportedly spent a whopping 19 weeks at the top. For the show’s penultimate song, she brought Fender onstage to perform the folk-rock megahit, their voices melding smoothly as he plucked away on a Jazzmaster.</p><p>The song was part of a 19-track setlist of nostalgic R&B, pop and soul devoted to the act of opening oneself up to love and all of the joys, pains and lessons learned along the way.</p><p><b></b> An early set highlight came when Dean and her background singers layered flawless harmonies for “Lady Lady,” her singers keeping time with shakers, adding texture to an already well-rounded full-band sound. <b></b></p><p>Just about every song came with an introduction from Dean, who would share its meaning or root. “The Art of Loving” was inspired by reading bell hooks’ “All About Love,” she said.</p><p>“The truest way to really love someone in your life is to want them to be the best version of themselves,” she explained, paraphrasing hooks. “Everyone here deserves to be loved that way, and I deserve that too.”</p><p><b></b> On “Let Alone the One You Love,” she sang a scorned lover’s waltz while the audience rocked back and forth, many with eyes closed and brows furrowed with feeling. “Who would do that to a friend? Let alone the one you love?” she sang, face pained, arms open. <b></b></p><p>Dean’s live band Saturday also breathed new life into the singer’s earlier material, including “Ladies Room” and “Carmen,” from her 2023 debut “Messy.” Dean said the latter ballad was about her grandmother, who immigrated to the U.K. from Guyana at just 18. Dean declared the song a celebration of her grandmother’s life and dedicated it to all grandmothers and immigrants.</p><p>“I don’t understand why we’ve all become so fearful of each other — we’re all just people,” she said before her grandmother’s voice played over the speakers to start the song, recounting her journey.</p><p>Another standout moment came during her performance of “A Couple of Minutes,” during which her band interpolated chords from the underrated 1970s soul gem “We Had True Love” by Hot Chocolate. Asking if anyone had been through a breakup recently, Dean said the song is about forgiveness, acceptance and remembering that “just because something didn’t last forever that doesn’t mean it was a waste of your time … anytime you get to fall in love, that was time well spent.”</p><p><b> </b>“F--- my ex!” one crowdgoer yelled to a friend before belting out the song’s chorus with seemingly everyone else in the crowd. <b></b></p><p>Dean fortified the night’s ’70s soul connections with a cover of Curtis Mayfield’s masterpiece “Move on Up” — a bold move in the legend’s hometown. But Dean stuck the landing, also using the song to introduce her band while she jumped and twirled in the reflective light of a disco ball spinning from above the stage.</p><p>It all led up to the night’s closer, “Man I Need.” Dean leapt exuberantly as she sang, sending the fringes of her sparkling dress swaying. Amplified by additional horn arrangements and a singalong, the number was a kind of joyful denouement after a set’s worth of emotions.</p><p>As fireworks burst above, fans lifted their voices in what felt like the cathartic ending scene of a feel-good rom-com. Dean’s words, from earlier in the night, suddenly clicked in: “If you take anything from this show, it’s go and give the love you feel you deserve.”</p><h3>Set list</h3><p>Nice to Each Other<br>Lady Lady<br>So Easy (To Fall in Love)<br>Close Up<br>Let Alone the One You Love<br>Messy<br>Carmen<br>Echo<br>Time<br>A Couple Minutes<br>The Hardest Part<br>Baby Steps<br>Ladies Room<br>Move on Up (Curtis Mayfield cover)<br>OK Love You Bye<br>It Isn't Perfect But It Might Be<br>Dive<br>Rein Me In (with Sam Fender)<br>Man I Need</p>

entries.title: After acquiring starter Luis Castillo, White Sox GM Chris Getz is still looking to deal
entries.summary: <p>ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — White Sox general manager Chris Getz is anteing up before the trade deadline, and he said he’s looking to put more chips on the table — but not all of them.</p><p>Late Saturday, he turned one hand into Mariners right-hander Luis Castillo. On Sunday, he said he still was monitoring the catcher market and anticipated making a move. He also said the market for rental players came with exorbitant costs and he didn’t want to hinder Sox teams in 2027 and 2028.</p><p>So while it’s unlikely Getz will go all in, he’s staying at the table.</p><p>“I don’t take any of this for granted,” he said.</p><p>Nor should he. Seasons like the one the Sox are experiencing are precious, and they still can help themselves before the deadline at 5 p.m. Monday. They took a big step toward improving their pitching staff by acquiring Castillo, a three-time All-Star who can give the Sox length and playoff experience, two things the rotation lacks.</p><p>Getz gave up veteran reliever Seranthony Dominguez, who lost the closer job, and two prospects, catcher Boston Smith and outfielder Nolan Jones. Smith was the Sox’ 15th-ranked prospect, according to MLB.com, and Getz views him as a future major-leaguer, just not this season or next. The Sox acquired Jones from the Guardians in June.</p><p>The most interesting part of the deal was the financial aspect. In a very un-Sox-like move, they took on the remainder of Castillo’s hefty contract, which runs through next season. That means they’re paying what’s left of the $22.75 million Castillo is owed this year and all of it next year, totaling about $30 million. He also has a $25 million vesting option for 2028 if he throws 180 innings in 2027.</p><p>Castillo, 33, is in the fold for the Sox’ surprisingly open competitive window, which is being propped up by slugger Munetaka Murakami. He has one year left on his $34 million contract, and his next deal could triple that. It would be an even more un-Sox-like move to give a $100 million contract, considering they’re one of three MLB teams that never has done that.</p><p>So it’s important for Getz to act now, because it would be very Sox-like to push away from the table after dealing for Castillo, doing just enough to make the team better but not enough to push it over the top. Getz said the biggest motivating factor in making the deal was the big bump Castillo gave the Sox’ playoff probability this year and next. Imagine if Getz does more.</p><p>The Sox think they can help Castillo, who has what would be a career-worst 5.06 ERA. Getz blamed the piggyback role Castillo played out of the bullpen for much of the season before resuming his typical starter’s routine. Getz pointed to the Sox’ work with fireballing veteran Jordan Hicks, who has been lights-out lately, as evidence of what they could do for Castillo.</p><p>Getz also raved about Castillo’s reputation and the type of teammate he is. He figures to blend in with players who have formed a tight-knit group. Getz said that was important to him.</p><p>“I am sensitive to the clubhouse and not being disruptive to this group because they've done something really special,” he said. “Trying to find ways to really fuel this club without disrupting the chemistry that clearly exists within this clubhouse.”</p><p>Getz is saying everything Sox fans want to hear. But to ensure the Sox maintain their hold on first place in the American League Central, there’s more he can do. The team chose to move Erick Fedde to the bullpen and keep rookie Noah Schultz in the rotation, despite an erratic season. Another quality veteran starter would help.</p><p>After three consecutive seasons with 100-plus losses, the Sox aren’t asking fans for patience anymore. Even Getz sounds more practical than patient. But to take even more advantage of the hand he has been dealt, he needs to put in a few more chips.</p><div class="PageListL" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" entries.title: Pete Crow-Armstrong's refined approach continues impressing Cubs manager Craig Counsell
entries.summary: <p>Before this season, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> center fielder <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs/2026/07/25/cubs-pete-crow-armstrong-mvp-paul-skenes-pirates-cy-young-ian-happ-matthew-boyd-shota-imanaga" ><b>Pete Crow-Armstrong</b></a><b> </b>had walked 53 times in 293 career games.</p><p>He’s already at 59 walks with 50 games left in 2026.</p><p>Crow-Armstrong walked three times Sunday, including twice against former Cy Young Award winner <b>Gerrit Cole</b>. Over the three trips to the plate that ended with walks, Crow-Armstrong saw 25 pitches.</p><p>Manager <b>Craig Counsell </b>said Crow-Armstrong had “excellent” at-bats, swinging at and taking the right pitches. That started with his first at-bat, when he saw 10 Cole deliveries and successfully challenged on a 3-2 slider to reach base.</p><p>“The first at-bat is great,” Counsell said. “You throw up a 10-pitch walk on a starter for a game, it’s almost like you’ve taken an inning away from him. You’ve reduced the threat of seven innings [from the starter].”</p><p>It’s quite a departure from what Crow-Armstrong was in the past: a free-swinger who only walked occasionally. The transformation has impressed Counsell.</p><p>“That’s an incredible athlete, good baseball player,” Counsell said. “It’s a young man getting better at the game.”</p><p>Crow-Armstrong wasn’t as effusive about the day. He was disappointed the Cubs offense didn’t support starter <b>Colin Rea </b>and the pitching staff, and seemed unsatisfied with his own output.</p><p>“Today is a day where critical me would just be thinking about putting balls in play instead of just walking, and being on second base,” Crow-Armstrong said. “I’m just slightly bummed with the runs that we put up today just because our guys went out there and threw the [heck] out of the ball the last two days, but today specifically.”</p><p>The Cubs were 1 for 9 with runners in scoring position and left eight runners on base.</p><h2><b>Challenging moment</b></h2><p>The Cubs should have tied the game in the sixth.</p><p>They had loaded the bases with two outs and second baseman <b>Nico Hoerner </b>was facing Yankees reliever <b>Brent Headrick</b>. Hoerner jumped ahead 3-0 and Headrick delivered a 94 mph four-seam fastball that appeared to be outside.</p><p>Home plate umpire <b>Scott Barry </b>called the pitch a strike and Hoerner did not challenge. On the next pitch, Hoerner flew out to center field to end the Cubs’ threat.</p><p>“I’m sure Nico has looked at it and is wishing he would have challenged,” Counsell said.</p><p>Despite having a good sense of the strike zone, Hoerner has struggled with the new review system. He’s only been successful on six of his 14 challenges this season.</p><h2><b>Rea’s day</b></h2><p>Rea struck out a season-high seven batters over 5 2/3 innings, including the first five hitters. He has a 3.20 ERA over his last eight starts, and has worked at least five innings in those outings.</p><p>The only real mistake Rea made was in the third when he gave up a two-run home run to New York’s <b>Jose Caballero</b>. Rea had been succeeding with his four-seam fastball and went to it down 1-0 in the count.</p><p>Caballero didn’t miss it, and delivered the Yankees’ only runs.</p><p>“Unfortunately, that was the game,” Rea said.</p><h2><b>Officially the end</b></h2><p>The Cubs traded <b>Jameson Taillon </b>and cash considerations to the Blue Jays for a player to be named later or cash. Taillon, who was wrapping up a four-year, $68 million contract, was designated for assignment last Monday.</p>

entries.title: Jones prepares to launch newest Public League football program
entries.summary: <p>The turf field at Jones’ athletic complex in the South Loop is lined for multiple sports, but it never has been used for football games.</p><p>That will change when the Eagles launch the Public League’s newest program this month.</p><p>By CPS policy, Jones will begin play as a junior-varsity program, with its debut set for Aug. 22 at Hersey. The Eagles will play Ridgewood’s varsity in Week 2, followed by seven more JV games against Public League foes.</p><p>Until now, Jones — with an enrollment of 1,912 — was the largest Public League school without football.</p><p>That has changed because of Frank Dickerson, the school’s head of security and the first head coach of the program.</p><p>Dickerson played football at now-closed Hope in Englewood before walking on at Illinois State. He got into coaching at Hope more than 15 years ago and worked with current Payton coach Calvin Clark there, as well as at Sullivan and Payton. He also coached in the Denver area before returning to Chicago in 2020.</p><p>When he got to Jones, Dickerson asked why the Eagles didn’t have a program. He was told school officials were open to the idea but didn’t want to have a coach use the job simply to pad a résumé and move on.</p><p>‘‘I’m like, ‘Well, I’m embedded in here,’ and I had the ears of the students, staff and faculty,’’ he said.</p><p>He was asked to submit a four-year plan for the program. Two weeks later, he did that one better by producing a five-year plan, ‘‘just to let them know I was very serious about what I was doing.’’</p><p>During summer workouts, the Eagles had almost 40 players. Dickerson expects that number to rise when school starts and more freshmen join the team.</p><p>One challenge now: Fewer than 10 players have previous football experience. But Dickerson isn’t fazed.</p><p>‘‘I think another reason I got the job [is] I’m a developer,’’ he said. ‘‘Everywhere I’ve gone, it’s been an OK [or] subpar team or nonexistent, almost. I’ve gone in there, and we had great success because it’s about patience and understanding that you’re going to go through trials and tribulation. But your patience is<br>going to be rewarded by their play, eventually.’’</p><p>While Dickerson takes the long view, the future is now for a lot of his players. The junior class is the biggest on the roster, but there also are more than a dozen seniors who won’t be around when the Eagles move to a full varsity schedule.</p><p>That doesn’t bother senior running back/linebacker Jaylen Trice.</p><p>‘‘We’re leaving a legacy,’’ he said. ‘‘And even though it is a JV schedule, our names are going to be written down in history. This is the first year for a lot of us. So the way I look at it is, we are walking so the [next] people out there can run.’’</p><p>Shawn Slaughter, another senior running back/linebacker, expects this experience to help prepare him for life after high school.</p><p>‘‘The main reason I wanted to play football was to see what that mindset is like to try to build a tougher mentality, something I can carry throughout the rest of my life, being able to persevere and push through,’’ he said.</p><p>Senior tight end/lineman TJ Dumas wanted to play football ‘‘to give myself some structure. . . . This program has definitely helped me, making sure I can be at a certain place every time, every day, making sure I eat right.</p><p>‘‘Also, I’ve always liked football since I was young, and I was waiting for Jones to get a football team. And it finally came.’’<br></p>

entries.title: Dodgers getting Tarik Skubal only makes Cubs' road tougher
entries.summary: <p>When <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/cubs" >Cubs</a> manager Craig Counsell found out the Dodgers were getting Tarik Skubal from the Tigers, his reaction was quite measured.</p><p>“I was half-asleep and fell asleep five minutes later,” Counsell said Sunday morning before the Cubs lost 2-1 to the Yankees.</p><p>Counsell might not have been alarmed enough to interrupt his night’s slumber, but Los Angeles grabbing another prized asset makes the task ahead tougher for the Cubs.</p><p>No matter what, it was going to be difficult for the Cubs to win the 2026 World Series. The National League is loaded, the journey through three or four playoff rounds is filled with traps and variance and the Cubs’ starting rotation has been hit with multiple injuries.</p><p>And even if Jed Hoyer and the Cubs get a starter or two before Monday’s trade deadline, they won’t match what the Dodgers did. By snagging Skubal, Los Angeles fortified itself for a run at a third straight championship by importing a lefthander who led the American League in both ERA-plus and fielding independent pitching in 2024 and 2025. The Dodgers also made sure a horde of challengers interested in Skubal – reportedly including the Cubs – wouldn’t add the most coveted arm available.</p><p>Though nothing is guaranteed in the playoffs, there’s a good chance any team that wants to represent the NL in the World Series will have to beat the Dodgers. Already a steep climb, that’s become more challenging after the Dodgers added another superstar to the mega-team that already had Shohei Ohtani, Freddie Freeman, Mookie Betts, Yoshinobu Yamamoto and plenty more.</p><p>The Cubs are getting a look at that this week at Wrigley Field, including Skubal’s Dodgers debut Tuesday. But an early-August series isn’t the same as having to get past that group in the postseason.</p><p>“If you’re going to win a World Series and accomplish the things that we want to, you’re going to have to beat good players and good teams no matter what,” second baseman Nico Hoerner told the Sun-Times. [The Dodgers trading for Skubal] doesn’t change too much on our end as far as what we can control.”</p><p>Center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong said he didn’t have a reaction to the Skubal news. The trade, Crow-Armstrong said, had nothing to do with him.</p><p>“It will be fun to face him [Tuesday],” Crow-Armstrong said. “I haven’t gotten to face him since last year. A big fan of his as a person and as a competitor as well. So, I mean, cool.”</p><p>Hoerner and Crow-Armstrong’s reactions aren’t surprising. Competitors at the big-league level will say they’re concerned only about their own teams, not the actions of other franchises.</p><p>Yet the facts are there: the best team adding maybe the best pitcher in the world will not make it easier for anybody to beat the Dodgers. That includes the Cubs, who should be getting some help.</p><p>“There’s been so much criticism on the pitching staff, who’s really managed to throw a lot of really good games for us. There was a lot of criticism when we weren’t really putting up runs and we weren’t really winning games,” Crow-Armstrong said. “We’ve still put ourselves in a position to go get some pieces that would only end up helping this squad. We’re already in really good shape in terms of who we have and the type of people that we have, the type of competitors.</p><p>“Any addition would be that. It would be great,” Crow-Armstrong continued. “We’ll see what happens, but we’ve still got to go play ball, so whatever happens, happens.”</p><p>Eventually, that could mean Skubal and the Dodgers standing in the Cubs’ October path.</p>

entries.summary: <p>Cruz Beckham got his first taste of the stage 18 years ago. His mom Victoria Beckham, aka Posh Spice, was performing with the Spice Girls at Madison Square Garden, and the then-3-year-old <a class="Link" href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KoZ7a_nCPLQ&t=5s" target="_blank" >busted out breakdancing</a> in front of 20,000 people, prompting Posh to declare him the “next Justin Timberlake.”</p><p>That he is not. entries.title: White Sox move Erick Fedde to bullpen, keep Noah Schultz in rotation after Luis Castillo trade
entries.summary: <p>ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Erick Fedde wasn’t thrilled being moved to the bullpen after the White Sox acquired Luis Castillo from the Mariners, but he has been so accommodating during this surprisingly successful season, he wasn’t going to stop now.</p><p>“They just told me [they] wanted to switch my role to the pen and keep me stretched out,” Fedde said of his meeting Sunday with coaches. “And I said, ‘All right, let’s do it.’ ”</p><p>“He understood,” manager Will Venable said. “He views himself as a starting pitcher, and I think there’s some disappointment with that. At the same time, I know more than anything he wants to help our team win, and if that means changing roles, ultimately he’s on board with that.”</p><p>Rookie Noah Schultz will stay in the rotation — for now. At 88 innings with the Sox and Triple-A Charlotte, he’s one-third of an inning shy of his career high. The Sox want to maintain Fedde’s length, but Venable admitted it’ll be tough to do out of the pen. Fedde isn’t concerned the move will affect his performance. He has lowered his ERA from a season-high 5.47 in May to 4.13.</p><p>“Luckily, I’ve had those experiences in my career,” he said. “You’ve got to be a little more focused on prep and make sure you’re keeping yourself in a good position. Maybe it’s a little harder on the body. If they’re keeping me stretched out, it shouldn’t hopefully be too bad.”</p><p>Fedde allowed one run in five innings with six strikeouts in his last start, a 6-1 victory Friday against the Rays.</p><p>As for Castillo, he'll make his Sox debut Thursday in the series finale in Boston. Davis Martin will start Tuesday, and Massachusetts native Sean Burke will start Wednesday.</p><h3>‘Everything’ works for Kay in win</h3><p>Anthony Kay threw a career-high 6 ⅓ innings and didn’t allow a run, and the Sox hit three homers to rout the Rays 9-1 and take the three-game set from the American League leaders. The Sox outscored the Rays 15-3 for the series, which drew a sizable contingent of Sox fans.</p><p>Kay allowed seven hits, and the only walk he allowed was to the last batter he faced. Venable said Kay had “everything” working for him in his 89 pitches, but Kay made particular mention of his cutter.</p><p>“That’s my go-to pitch, getting the cutter in on guys,” he said. “I think a lot of the success today was with that. Getting the cutter in leads to being able to use the changeup more and the four-seam [fastball] up. When that thing’s working, that’s when I’m at my best.”</p><p>Andrew Benintendi, Everson Pereira and Miguel Vargas went deep. Pereira was inserted into the lineup late when right fielder Braden Montgomery was scratched because of a skin infection on his right ankle. Pereira went 2-for-4 with a double that snapped an 0-for-20 skid, the homer and four RBI. Montgomery is expected to be fine.</p><p>Tristan Peters snapped an 0-for-24 skid with a single in the fourth. He also walked in the sixth.</p><h3>Smith, McDougal adjusting to pen</h3><p>The Sox are preparing Triple-A left-hander Hagen Smith and right-hander Tanner McDougal — their Nos. 2 and 4 prospects, respectively — for bullpen roles this season. Both are coming off injuries, but Sox director of player development Paul Janish said they’re in good shape.</p><p>“Being able to not worry about five innings and being able to empty the tank for five or six outs is something that they’re adjusting to,” Janish said. “But they’re both doing really well — healthy, which is the most important thing. Assuming that health, I think they’re both going to get a chance to perform at the major-league level this year.”</p><p>General manager Chris Getz mentioned his excitement to see them in the Sox’ bullpen. Next season, both will be built up to start, Janish said.</p><div class="PageListL" data-module data-hide-authors="true" data-hide-categories="true" data-hide-dates="true" data-show-loadmore="true" entries.title: Review: Destin Conrad shines in star-making set at Lollapalooza
entries.summary: <p>When discussing his Grammy-nominated debut album, “Love on Digital,” with Billboard, Destin Conrad called the sound “loud” and “queer.” Those are also fitting descriptors for his set on the Allianz stage at Lollapalooza on Sunday. But you could also add “unapologetically Black.”</p><p>The 26-year-old Florida native demonstrated his deep understanding of multiple Black art forms, performing R&B tracks from the aforementioned “Love on Digital,” and jazz tunes from his new album, “wHIMSY,” Oh, and he showed that he can also make irresistible island music; he played a song from his forthcoming reggae album, which he casually announced that he is dropping this month.</p><p>That versatility, along with his humor and natural performance ability onstage, is why he’s such an exciting new talent — co-signed by everyone from Kehlani to Meshell Ndegeocello. (He is a guest on the latter singer’s upcoming duets album, “Synonym.”) And he drew one of Lollapalooza’s most diverse crowds of the weekend.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div is intended to appear thrown together but clearly demonstrates his eye for fashion. His rich, smoky vocals were supported by a competent band, including a standout bass player and keyboardist who also performed a killer sax solo. The audience enthusiastically sang along to every song, especially the crowd-pleasing “Bad B------ and “Kissing in Public.”</p><p>At the end of the set, the sun emerged from the clouds, as if to herald the rising of a new star. And by the lyrics of his song, “So Nice,” Conrad knows it, too. “It's OK, it's all right/My life is so nice.”<br></p>
